To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a tunable ring resonator based on a conductor/ferroelectrics/dielectric structure that is tunable over a large bandwidth with a high Q factor.
the change in the dielectric constant of SrTiO 3 can be used to tune the resonance frequency of a ring resonator by 12% at Ku-band frequencies.
the performance of Au/ferroelectric thin film conductor/ ferroelectric/dielectic tunable ring resonator can be improved by applying a bias between the ring and the microstrip line.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication, and characterization of tunable microstrip ring resonators.
the development of tunable microwave components based on the ferroelectric properties of SrTiO 3 (STO) and the conductor/ferroelectricsuperstrate (CFS) effect in Au/STO/LaAlO 3 (LAO) structures.
the development of tunable microwave devices based on ferroelectric thin films.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the biasing scheme is a key factor in the design of tunable resonator devices based on SrTiO3 ferroelectric thin films.
the biasing scheme used for the tunable ring resonator is critical for the performance of these devices.
these tunable ring resonator circuits are very promising candidates for the development of tunable filters and oscillators.

the performance of the rings is strongly dependent on the biasing scheme.
the use of a ferroelectric material as an active component in microwave devices can be an alternative to other tunable materials.

it is possible to tune the resonant frequency of a ring resonator using a dc bias applied to the ferroelectric film.
